style=\"text-align: justify;\">\u003Cstrong>Taylor Bastien \u003C/strong>became the 11th head coach in UNH women's lacrosse program history on August 2, 2024. has been head coach at Bentley University, her alma mater, the previous seven seasons (2018-24). She led the Falcons to their first two NCAA tournament appearances (2021, 2024) as well as their first Northeast-10 Conference championship (2021).\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nBentley was ranked in the final Intercollegiate Women’s Lacrosse Coaches Association Division II Top 25 Poll all seven seasons of her tenure, including No. 16 in 2024 and a program-best No. 12 in 2021. Bastien guided the Falcons to an overall record of 63-43 (.594 win percentage) with a pair of wins against top-10 teams in 2023. Bentley recorded a .667 conference winning percentage (48-24 record) under Bastien.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nIn seven seasons, Bastien coached 27 all-conference selections, 11 all-region honorees, a two-time All-American who was named the Division II Goalie of the Year (2021), and another All-American who was named the NE10 Attacker of the Year and New England Lacrosse Journal Division II Player of the Year in ‘24.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nHer student-athletes also excelled academically, as Bentley was named an IWLCA Academic Honor Squad every year. The Falcons earned the Team Academic Award from the NE10 for having the best combined GPA of women’s lacrosse teams in the conference in both the 2022-23 and 2023-24 academic years, and the team recorded a perfect 100 percent graduation rate in the most recent NCAA Academic Success Rate report (December 2023).\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nBastien was head coach at Simmons College from August 2015 to January 2018 and led the team to the conference championship game in 2017. Her collegiate coaching career began September 2014 as an assistant coach at the University of Bridgeport, where she spent one year before joining the Simmons staff.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nAs a student-athlete, Bastien was one of the top point producers in Bentley history. She recorded 99 goals and 121 assists for a total of 220 points to rank second in assists and third in points in the program’s annals.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nThe four-year standout was a captain in 2013, led the Falcons to the NE10 playoffs all four years, led the team in points twice (2013, 2014), and recorded both the second and third most assists in a single season in program history with 42 in 2012 and 41 in 2014.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nBastien’s collegiate accolades include All-Conference Second Team as a senior in 2014 and she was selected to play in the IWLCA North/South All-Star Senior Game.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nBastien graduated with a Bachelor of Science in Management in 2013 and went on to earn an MBA in Marketing from Bentley in 2014.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\n“Taylor possesses the values, competitive spirit, and winning pedigree that align with our vision for the UNH lacrosse program,” UNH Director of Athletis Allison Rich said. “She built a winning program at Bentley the right way, demanding excellence of her team without compromising the importance of academic success and the student-athlete experience. I know she will energize our alumnae and supporters and bring our program back to prominence while continuing to develop Wildcats for Life.”\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cstrong>\u003Cu>Taylor Bastien File\u003C/u>\u003C/strong>\u003Cbr />\r\nEducation:\u003Cbr />\r\n   Bentley University, B.S. style=\"text-align: justify;\">\u003Cstrong>Evan Gray ’19\u003C/strong> joined the administrative team as the Assistant Athletic Director, Student-Athlete Wellness and Academic Support Services, in June 2023. In this role, Evan provides a wide array of support to student-athletes in terms of student-athlete wellness and academic support. He coordinates and facilitates educational programming to assist in the personal and professional development of all student-athletes. Topics covered include, but are not limited to, career placement, student-athlete welfare, leadership development, community involvement, mentoring, financial management, sexual assault and violence prevention, and stress/time management. From an academic standpoint, he mentors, counsels, and provides proactive monitoring to student-athletes to ensure academic success.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nPrior to his return to Durham, Evan worked at Florida State University as the Student-Athlete Academic Services (SAAS) Assistant Academic Advisor (2022-23). In that role he monitored progress toward degree and eligibility for Seminole football student-athletes, delivered football tutor summary reports to academic advisors and learning specialists, and collaborated with the Leaders Yearning for Excellence (LYFE): Beyond the Spear program. The LYFE program was built to promote the social, intellectual and academic well-being of Black male student-athletes.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nEvan earned his Master of Science degree in Athletic Leadership from Clemson University in 2022. While at Clemson, Evan was a student intern in the Passionate About Winning (PAW) Journey program. This position involved collaborating with colleagues to assist Clemson football players in creating resumes, cover letters and LinkedIn profiles. He created PAW Journey promotional material and gave tours to recruits and stakeholders. Previously, he was a student intern in the athletic marketing department, where he assisted in the development, coordinator and implementation of marketing and promotional efforts for Tiger Athletics programs.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nEvan earned his Bachelor of Science degree in Kinesiology: Sport Studies with a minor in Business Administration from UNH in 2019.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nThe Centreville, Va., native was a running back for the Wildcat football team from 2015-19. As a senior captain, he earned \u003Ca href=\"https://unhwildcats.com/news/2019/11/26/six-cats-receive-caa-football-all-conference-award.aspx\">CAA All-Conference First Team\u003C/a> honors when he carried the ball 108 times for 646 rushing yards and four touchdowns, both of which were team highs. He ranked No. 2 on the CAA leaderboard in yards per carry and eighth in rushing yards per game.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr />\r\nAt the 2020 Senior Showcase, Evan earned the University’s \u003Ca href=\"https://unhwildcats.com/news/2020/5/7/general-unh-celebrates-outstanding-performances-with-virtual-senior-showcase.aspx\">Tina True Award\u003C/a> for his dedication to the strength and conditioning program.\u003Cbr />\r\n \u003Cbr
